prompts: We want a 3D scene someone would keep as a wallpaper: the classic view of Mount Fuji at dusk, with the red five-tier Chureito pagoda and cherry trees in bloom, in a low poly look with some gentle motion. Deliver it as {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code and no external models or textures. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
Now verifying it renders in a real browser:It renders, but composition and lighting need tuning: the pagoda and trees are far too small against Fuji, the scene is too dark, and petals are invisible at that scale. Revising:That looks like a stale screenshot; reloading the page:Trees are buried inside the hills (they sit at y=0) and the snow cap is hidden inside the cone. Fixing geometry placement:Snow cap slope mismatch creates a "brim", and the peak is cut off. Matching the snow cone slope to Fuji's and reframing the camera:Close. Final polish: brighter snow, bigger pagoda clear of the tree cluster, reposition sun:Composition is good. Final verification — console errors and that motion actually animates (two frames differ):Done.

**[goal]** A single-file, no-build low-poly dusk wallpaper of Mount Fuji with the five-tier Chureito pagoda and blooming cherry trees, delivered as `./scene/index.html`.

**[action]** Built everything procedurally in three.js 0.170.0 (loaded from the one allowed jsdelivr URL; Google Fonts supplies the Cormorant Garamond title; no models, textures, or other network calls). Scene contents: vertex-gradient dusk sky dome, flat-shaded low-poly Fuji (jittered cone) with a slope-matched snow cap, five-tier pagoda with roofs and golden sorin finial on a terrace hill, ~32 cherry trees (trunk + faceted blossom icosahedra), foreground hills, lake, sun disc, and 260 instanced falling petals. Gentle motion: slow camera drift with mouse parallax, tree sway, petal fall.

**[result]** Verified live in a browser by opening the file directly (no build step): it renders the composed scene shown above, and I confirmed (1) zero JS errors in the page, and (2) real animation — petal positions visibly change between frames/screenshots, and the sway code runs on a clock loop. Composition was tuned over two revision rounds against screenshots: fixed trees buried inside terrain, a snow "brim" from mismatched cone slopes, and a cut-off peak.

**[next]** Assumptions I chose, since the brief left them open: dusk = sun low on the left with purple-to-amber sky; pagoda placed left-of-center on a terrace as in the classic photograph; motion kept subtle (wallpaper-appropriate); title text overlays the scene and can be deleted from the `.title` div if you want a pure wallpaper. Known limitation: the snow cap reads faintly at dusk lighting — if you want a brighter snowline, raise the `emissiveIntensity` on the snow material in `scene/index.html`.
